text:
priya: Quick question — before we flip v2 default routing, we need to decide autoswitch thresholds and what shows up in Console. Proposal: route 30% to v2, if error rate > 2% for 5m, switch those requests back to v1 for that customer for 10m. Telemetry: surface per-customer error-rate, avg-latency, and token-cost delta. Thoughts? @sasha @ben

ben: +1 on a conservative canary. Couple concerns: how do we compute "error rate" (5xx only? hallucination signals?) and how do we avoid oscillation across short spikes?

sasha: From UX/product POV we need a clear indicator in the Console per-route: status (v1/v2), last flip reason, and time-to-eligible-for-retry. Users will yell if it silently moves.

maria: For runtime, easiest is to track transport-level errors (5xx, connection resets, timeouts). We can also emit a separate quality signal later (eval hooks). To prevent oscillation we should use a sliding window + cool-down. Proposed: 5m window, threshold 2%, cool-down 10m. Matches Priya's suggestion.

kevin: Observability notes: we should expose two telemetry streams: "routing.decisions" (per-request: route, final-backend) and "routing.metrics" (aggregates per-customer, per-route: qps, p50/p95 latency, 5xx_rate, token_cost_avg). That way Console can query aggregates and we keep raw decision log for audits.

priya: Agreed. How would the policy look in config? Something lightweight like:

```yaml
autoswitch_policy:
  rollout_percent: 30
  error_window_sec: 300 # 5m
  error_threshold_pct: 2
  cool_down_sec: 600 # 10m
  backfill_to: v1
```

ben: That looks fine. Two additional asks: 1) quota/commit impact — when requests are moved to v2, cost per-token may change and we need to reflect that in billing estimates. 2) telemetry retention — keep routing.decisions for 30d, aggregates longer.

kevin: We'll implement routing.decisions -> kafka topic with 30d retention and routing.metrics -> long-term TSDB. Console will read metrics for dashboards.

rollout-bot: Canary for v2_autoswitch_policy started by @priya — 30% traffic, group-based.

maria: Implementation question: when we flip back to v1 for a customer, do we pin them to v1 for all routes or just the failing route? I vote per-route to minimize blast radius.

sasha: Per-route makes sense. Also need a UI affordance: "Force opt-in to v2" and "Disable autoswitch for this customer" for enterprise customers.

ben: Also consider a telemetry flag to mark "policy-engaged" so support can filter tickets. e.g., routing.metrics includes labels: policy=autoswitch, policy_reason=error_rate.

priya: Next steps: (a) eng-runtime implement policy + per-route pinning (owner: maria), (b) metrics pipeline work (owner: kevin), (c) Console UX: status card + action buttons (owner: sasha), (d) doc + rollout runbook (owner: ben). I'll open a shallow RFC and link here.

maria: I'll start a small PR with the policy evaluator and simulation tests against historical telemetry to validate thresholds.

kevin: I'll wire up the topics and a dashboard prototype in Grafana and add a Console widget endpoint.

ben: I'll draft the runbook, include rollback steps and how to interpret the new metrics.

priya: Thanks. If no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll kick off the canary.

sasha: +1. Also adding a tiny UX note: show "last routed to v2: N minutes" and an explicit "why" tooltip (error rate / user-forced).

rollout-bot: Canary update: 30% ramp reached, 10m stable window starting now.

ben: One last thought — add a debug flag to replay routing.decisions for a customer id in DevConsole to repro. Will be useful for support.

priya: Nice. I'll add that to the RFC. Closing thread for decisions; we'll keep the chat for implementation questions.
